messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: [Name], [Age]-year-old female

Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]

Chief Complaint:
Left supraclavicular and axillary painful lump

Hospital Course and Treatment:
The patient was admitted to the Hematologic Clinic with a painful left supraclavicular and axillary lump. She had received the first dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine five days prior to presentation. The patient experienced injection site pain, headaches, chills, and a sense of “heaviness” of the neck and upper chest for two days after injection that gradually resolved. On physical examination and Doppler ultrasound, multiple enlarged lymph nodes were seen in the axillary, supraclavicular, and low lateral neck areas. Painful axillary lymphadenopathy also appeared after the second dose of the vaccine. No other abnormal findings were noted. Blood tests including full chemistry, blood count, and CRP levels were within normal limits. The patient was treated with pain relief medication and her symptoms improved gradually until complete resolution.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient responded well to pain relief medication and her symptoms gradually resolved over time. No complications were reported during hospitalization.

Follow-Up Plan:
The patient will be discharged with instructions to follow up with her primary care physician for any concerns or symptoms in the future. No further follow-up is required at this time.

Summary:
This is a case of a healthy middle-aged woman who presented with an adverse reaction to the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine resulting in painful axillary lymphadenopathy. The patient was treated with pain relief medication, and her symptoms resolved over time with no complications identified during hospitalization. The patient will be discharged with instructions to follow up with her primary care physician for any concerns or symptoms in the future.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is reactive lymphadenopathy, a painful enlargement of axillary and supraclavicular nodes caused by an adverse reaction to the COVID-19 vaccine. Lymphadenopathy sits in chapter R, but in ICD-10-AM an adverse effect of a correctly administered vaccine is coded to the manifestation. Here the manifestation is localized lymph node enlargement, R59, with the vaccine adverse effect recorded separately as an external cause (Y59). The alternative, lymphadenitis I88 or L04 (acute lymphadenitis), is not supported because the nodes were reactive rather than infected, and the blood tests including CRP were normal. So the chapter is R and the category is R59.

CODE: R59
